{{distinguish|Dini criterion}}
In mathematics, the '''Dini–Lipschitz criterion''' is a [[sufficient condition]] for the [[Fourier series]] of a [[periodic function]] to [[uniform convergence|converge uniformly]] at all [[real numbers]]. It was introduced by {{harvs|txt|authorlink=Ulisse Dini|last=Dini|first=Ulisse |year=1872}}, as a strengthening of a weaker criterion introduced by {{harvs|txt|authorlink= Rudolf Lipschitz|last=Lipschitz|first=Rudolf |year=1864}}. The criterion states that the Fourier series of a periodic function ''f'' converges uniformly on the real line if 
:<math>\lim_{\delta\rightarrow0^+}\omega(\delta,f)\log(\delta)=0</math>
where <math>\omega</math> is the [[modulus of continuity]] of ''f'' with respect to <math>\delta</math>.
